measurementContract.canonicalWallSource: docs/spec/ci_acceptance_contract.md section 6 - wall_seconds = max(job.completed_at) - min(job.started_at) over jobs whose started_at and completed_at are both non-null

formulas.wallSeconds: max(completed_at) - min(started_at) over jobs with both timestamps
formulas.runnerSeconds: sum(max(0, completed_at - started_at)); skipped job contributes 0
formulas.queuedSeconds: sum(max(0, started_at - created_at)) over jobs with started_at; skipped job -> 0
formulas.worstJobQueuedSeconds: max over jobs of max(0, started_at - created_at); skipped job -> 0
formulas.admissionGateEntryQueuedSeconds: max(0, started_at - created_at) of the workflow entry job (`closure-deriver`)
formulas.percentile: Hyndman-Fan type 7; sorted values are whole seconds because every GitHub timestamp is whole seconds
formulas.mergesPerHour: |{c : c in first-parent main commits, |parents(c)| >= 2, c.committer.date in (t-W, t]}| / W(hours) - docs/spec/ci_critical_path_metric.md section 2.6

metricScoping.admissionGateEntryVsWorstJob: admissionGateEntryQueuedSeconds (closure-deriver) and worstJobQueuedSeconds are different quantities. The former is the runner assignment delay from merge queue dispatch -> gate entry job; the latter is the wait of the longest-queued job in the job graph (31 runs have 26 jobs, 1 run has 19 jobs). The latter grows as concurrency rises.
metricScoping.literalAdmissionCheckJob: For the last `admission-check` job that issues the required context, created_at -> started_at is only p50 3.0s / p95 39.0s / max 81.0s. Because it is a rollup job that appears only after the dependency graph finishes, using it as a queue delay metric understates the delay. The proxy for 'admission-gate queue wait' must use the entry job (closure-deriver).

ceilingComparison.reading: Measured 2.921/h is 43.5% of the theoretical ceiling. The ceiling dropping does not mean throughput is bound by capacity - the bottleneck is still not throughput but input (PR supply).

No double counting - 1478 job entries / 1478 distinct (run,job) pairs.

freeConcurrencyLimitReached.interpretation: The limit was actually reached, not just in theory. However, it was only 0.69% of the window, and both bursts lasted only minutes. The observed value 20 is a lower bound counting only merge_group workflows - PR-triggered runs use the same 20 slots, so actual concurrency may have been 20 or more, and because the limit clamps at 20, values above 20 are unobservable. That is, 'limit reached' is true, but 'the limit continuously constrained throughput' is a separate proposition, and the wait distribution below is counter-evidence.

timeoutEvictions.evidence: Among non-skipped jobs: 0 jobs with no started_at, 0 jobs waiting 600s or more, 0 jobs waiting 2700s (45 minutes) or more.
timeoutEvictions.note: Even the run closest to check_response_timeout_minutes 120 minutes is 17.4 minutes, 14.5% of the limit.

buildGroupConcurrency.reading: The dispatch ceiling 100 did not bind at all (peak 6). The maximum number of concurrently live merge_group workflow runs was 30. Raising the ceiling further would gain nothing.

saturationAndEviction.conclusion: There are 0 pieces of evidence that a candidate was discarded due to runner capacity saturation. The Free 20 limit was actually reached (0.69% of window), but even in that interval job wait peaked at 385s, 7x below the 45-minute discard threshold.

facts: n=32 completed runs (out of 34 merge groups). 16 success / 16 failure. run_attempt is 1 for all.

Maximum job queue wait 385s (publication-integrity `secret-scan`), 0 over 600s, 0 over 2700s. 0 discards from 45-minute runner non-assignment.
max wall 1044s = 17.4 minutes, 14.5% of check_response_timeout_minutes 120 minutes.
merges/hour 2.921 (13 / 4.45h, first-parent merge commits by committer.date). That is 43.5% of the theoretical ceiling 6.710/h.

afterArmObservation.statisticalStatus: Because n=32 >= 20, p50 and p95 are declared for all 5 metrics: wall/runner/queued/worst-job/entry-job. No metric is INCOMPLETE. However, the success/failure strata each have n=16 < 20, so strata p95 is not declared and is given only as a reference value (statistics.strata).
afterArmObservation.throughputCeilingTest: The c1 serialization ceiling is wall p50 496.0s (arm) -> 7.258/h, and the c100 ceiling is 536.5s -> 6.710/h. Because the ceiling itself dropped (parallelization did not reduce wall), a refutation of the form 'the ceiling was reached' does not hold. Measured 2.921/h falls short of both ceilings. That is, the throughput bottleneck is input, not capacity.
afterArmObservation.whatItDoesEstablish: At build concurrency 100: (1) the dispatch ceiling is not binding (peak 6), (2) the merge queue dispatches candidates immediately (queue dwell = wall), (3) 12 landings including all 7 required contexts succeeded, and (4) there are moments when the Free 20 concurrent execution limit is actually reached, but even then job wait does not exceed 385s and never reaches the discard threshold.

reopenConditions: In naturally occurring bursts, the share of samples where active jobs sit at 20 >= 30% AND queuedSeconds p95 > 300s AND 45-minute discards > 0
Or, at c100 arm n>=20, merges/hour does not increase versus c1 while queue backlog (number of queue entries) persists
A plan upgrade is considered only when the above conditions are met and a cost basis (per-seat, included compute) is presented together.

reopenConditionEvaluation.note: Reopen conditions are not relaxed at discretion. Each clause is evaluated as written, and unsatisfied clauses are stated explicitly. The conclusion is 'conditions not met' and is not rephrased as 'conditions were close'.

clauseB_queuedP95Over300s.explanation: Under the queuedSeconds (sum) definition it is satisfied at 1064.5s, but the sum double counts concurrent job waits and is not wall-contributing time. Under the worst-job definition, which can be attributed to wall, it is not satisfied at 210.9s. Because the truth of the clause flips depending on which definition is used, it is recorded as PARTIAL and not promoted to PASS.

condition1.conjunction: FALSE (clauseA FALSE, clauseC FALSE). Even if clauseB is true, this is an AND, so condition 1 does not hold.

condition2.explanation: This file does not measure an independent merges/hour for the c1 interval. The arm file has only 24h 2.417/h and 7d 1.393/h, and both include the c1 and c100 intervals together, so neither is a c1-only rate. Nor is a criterion (period and ratio) pre-registered for whether queue backlog 'persists'. It is left unevaluated.

condition3.explanation: The cost basis is a human owner judgment outside this slice's authority.

reasoning: If capacity saturation is defined as 'was the limit reached', the answer is 'yes' (peak 20). But that definition cannot justify a plan upgrade - even during the 111 seconds at the limit, job wait was at most 385s, 1/7 of the 45-minute discard threshold. The substantive criterion for saturation is whether the queue grows to the threshold, and that signal is 0 cases.

Two of the three clauses in reopen condition 1 (ratio 0.693% < 30%, discards 0) are false, and the truth of the remaining clause flips with the definition. Because it is an AND, it cannot be grounds for reopening. This judgment is not softened to 'conditions nearly met'.

worst single job queued p95 210.9s has more than 10x margin against both check_response_timeout 120 minutes and the 45-minute runner assignment threshold (210.9s vs 2700s = 12.8x, vs 7200s = 34x). There are 0 observations of a candidate discarded or cut by timeout due to wait.

Most of wall p50 536.5s is runner execution. Queue dwell p50 521.5s being nearly equal to wall means there is no dispatch delay after queue entry and wall is entirely gate execution. That is, the remaining delay comes from the admission-gate job graph (go-critical-lane shard), not from the merge queue or runner capacity.

merges/hour 2.921 is 43.5% of the theoretical ceiling 6.710. Not being pinned to the ceiling means input shortage, and queueSupply (20 PRs supplied, of which 12 landed through the queue) is the evidence. A plan upgrade does not touch this bottleneck.

The concurrency consumer is not admission-gate. At peak 20, 10 of the 20 jobs were publication-integrity workflows, and 5 of those were the license-scan-shards matrix (shard 0/1/2 x 2 groups). If limit pressure becomes a problem again, the target is the publication-integrity shard, not the merge queue.

confounds.detail: 16 of the 32 runs failed. Failure runs are wall p50 626.0s / worst-job queued p50 96.5s, success runs 479.5s / 38.0s. The pooled p50 536.5s / 70.0s represents neither.
confounds.handling: Reported separately in statistics.strata. Throughput and delay comparisons must read the strata separately.

confounds.detail: Identical to the confound already recorded in the arm file - the c2 arm spans 11-18 to 11-21, the c1 arm 15 samples over about 2 hours, and the c100 after arm 4.45 hours. The time-of-day distributions of the three intervals differ, so wall/queued differences cannot be asserted as a configuration effect.
confounds.handling: This file makes no before/after ratio claim. It reports only the c100 distribution.

confounds.detail: 34 merge groups came from 20 PRs. PR #313 was redispatched 4 times, #287 3 times, #307 3 times, and #312 3 times. Retries are repeated failures of the same PR and are not independent samples.
confounds.handling: Run-level statistics count runs as independent units (the cohort definition in contract section 1). No PR-level resampling was done.

confounds.detail: 1 of the 13 landings (#309) has neither a merge_group run nor an added_to_merge_queue event. merged_by is a human account.
confounds.handling: The numerator of merges/hour is 13 because it counts first-parent merge commits per the contract (section 2.6). Read as 'queue throughput', however, it overcounts by 1. This is stated in landedOutsideQueue. The cause is undetermined, so it is not asserted to be a bypass.

observationGaps: For an in-flight run, the check-run `output.summary` has no `run=`/`attempt=`/`conclusion=` lines until completion (observed on 44890062520 at cohort measurement time). After completion, `run=44890062520 attempt=1 conclusion=success` is recorded. A check-run -> workflow run join must tolerate the absence of these lines.

`removed_from_merge_queue` timeline events have no reason field (all 33 assayed are null). 'Removal due to merge' and 'dequeue/eviction' cannot be distinguished from events alone. Therefore queue drops are not asserted to be 0 - instead, added/removed counts were equal per PR, and classification used only whether the removal time is within a few seconds of mergedAt. For #268, #287, #306, #299 and others, repeated re-entry shows that dequeues occurred, but the reason is unknown.

Total concurrency was measured only for merge_group workflows. PR/push-triggered runs share the same 20 slots but were not included, so peak 20 is a lower bound. Because the limit clamps at 20, the actual value is unobservable.
Per-runner-label capacity (e.g. the limit of a specific runner pool) is not observed separately from the plan-wide concurrent execution limit.
The updated_at of both rulesets advanced after the window closed (2026-11-21T09:46:14Z/15Z), but there is no parameter change. The updating actor is not observable through the read-only API.
The path by which PR #309 landed without going through the merge queue is not observed. The ruleset bypass_actors is 0 and all 7 required contexts are unchanged. It is not asserted to be a bypass.

Classifying the causes of the 16 failures requires log attribution and is out of scope for this file. The arm file confounds.failureTaxonomyAdmissionGateMG_n50 classifies samples from before 11-21, so it is not applied unchanged to this cohort.

caveats: admission-gate-only queue wait and worst-job queue wait are different metrics. The value behind claims like 'queue wait p50 36 minutes -> 18 seconds' is the entry job (closure-deriver) wait, p50 17.5s / max 143.0s, while the cohort-wide worst-job wait is p50 70.0s / max 248.0s. The two figures must not be presented as the same thing.

queuedSeconds (sum) double counts concurrent job waits. With 26 jobs in parallel, if each job waits only 70s the sum becomes 291s. Therefore the queued/wall ratio (median 0.541) does not mean '54% of wall is queue wait' - the wall-attributable queue wait is p50 70.0s (about 13%) on a worst-job basis.

2 in-flight runs (44890062520, 44890395238) were excluded from the main statistics as of the cutoff. 44890062520 completed (success) during observation, and the n=33 sensitivity calculation including it is given alongside in cohort.sensitivity.
For an in-flight merge_group check-run, `output.summary` may lack `run=` lines until completion (observed on 44890062520). A consumer joining check-runs to workflow runs must handle this absence.

peak concurrent jobs 20 is a lower bound counting only merge_group-triggered workflows. PR/push-triggered runs share the same limit, so the actual value may be higher, but it is not observed because of the limit clamp.
The Free 20 limit was actually reached. This file does not claim 'the limit was not reached' - what it claims is that 'reaching the limit did not lead to sustained queue growth'.
runnerSeconds (sum) is larger than wall (892.5 vs 536.5). It is a sum over parallel execution and must not be added as a component of wall.
With the GitHub Actions runs API pagination limit of 1,000, only the latest 1,000 runs were observed (total 2,500). The observation window (05:13 to 09:40Z) falls well within them.
Because GitHub records job timestamps at second granularity, the base values for percentile computation are whole seconds. Only the type-7 interpolation results are shown with one decimal place.

The conclusion mapping for 45-minute discards is absent from the official documentation (NOT STATED). Discard detection was proxied by 'absence of started_at for a non-skipped job' and by per-job wait time, and both are 0 cases.
